title: AI Has a Power Problem: Why the U.S. Power Grid Can't Keep Up | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 69
summary: Kallo describes power, grid equipment and skilled labor as bottlenecks to AI construction and favors GE Vernova's long order cycle. He discusses Tesla autonomy and storage, predicts a potential SpaceX-Tesla combination, and explains tariff-driven solar uncertainty. Eisman owns GE Vernova, questions Tesla's valuation and autonomy promises, and adopts the power-and-labor constraint thesis without endorsing all guest forecasts.
assessment: Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Ben Kallo is the interviewed Baird analyst. Eisman asks questions, discloses GE Vernova ownership and closes with an explicit distinction between Kallo's bullish Tesla thesis and his own skepticism.
framework_points: Distinguish announced projects from funded, interconnected construction and avoid double counting.
Identify speed-to-power and firm capacity rather than nominal generating capacity alone.
Value long-cycle equipment with backlog, service revenue and delivery timing.
Separate an EV business valuation from autonomy and robotics optionality.
tools_and_charts: Power demand estimates in GW and energy output in TWh
GE Vernova segments, orders and delivery slots
transcript_cautions: Severe unit issues: captions give US capacity as 150 GW, reverse MW/GW conversion, and call the 30 GW annual estimate 30 MW in Eisman's closing summary. Audio confirmation is required before assigning these numerical errors to either speaker.
SMR first-unit timing is described as 2035, while OPG's published plan is 2030; distinguish analyst delay forecast from official schedule.
The closing summary says the guest likes no solar names, but Kallo explicitly says he recommends Nextpower.
